reviews.text:
Hi Andrés,
Thank you for your feedback and for trusting our team.

Hello,
Thank you very much for your feedback.

I brought my sick cat in, they charged me a fortune. The cat lost a leg, and they told me that sometimes happens in isolated cases, and that it was just her turn. The vet pressured me to amputate the leg that they themselves had lost. I spent a fortune and nothing happened. Luckily, I went to another vet who actually cared about my cat. I left with my sick cat, missing a leg, and having spent a fortune. Out of politeness, I'll refrain from using harsh words. My cat is alive but without a leg, despite all of you.

Hi Ricardo,
Thank you very much for your feedback.

Yesterday we visited for the first time, and I'd like to highlight Maria Rodriguez's excellent work, professionalism, patience, and love for animals. The gentleness with which she treated my dog ​​and the passion she exudes for her profession, respecting his pace so he felt comfortable and giving him a thorough check-up, were truly remarkable. Maria is a 10 out of 10 as a professional. Thank you.

After three days of my dog ​​suffering from diarrhea and vomiting, I went to the clinic to get her seen. The receptionist told me I didn't have an appointment and that they were fully booked, but that they could give me one for the next day.

I explained that this clinic is open 24/7 for any emergency. She considered my dog's condition not urgent and told me to come back the following day.

I didn't waste any time and took my pet, without an appointment, to my usual veterinarian, who saw her even though it was half an hour before closing time and his office was full.

A veterinary clinic, open 24 hours a day, every day of the year, cannot refuse to treat an animal, claiming it's not an emergency (the receptionist isn't a veterinarian and couldn't diagnose or know what was wrong with my dog).

I don't know if this is the clinic's protocol or if the person who attended to me at reception thought they worked at a beauty salon instead of an emergency veterinary clinic.

Please take note so you don't turn away any client who comes to your clinic seeking assistance for their sick animal.

I went to the emergency room with my cat Winnie and Dr. Laia took very good care of us, with great accuracy in diagnosing and proposing steps to follow. When I got home, the kitten was much better. Very grateful.
I took my HORIK ID card in for a dental cleaning and it wouldn't come out!!! "It's the worst thing I've ever done."

I would like to express my gratitude to the veterinarian Fran and the assistant Gabi, who from the very beginning have been very helpful both professionally and humanly in their treatment and fulfillment of their work. They have done everything possible to ensure that this visit and their empathy with my little dog has been of a delicacy and professionalism that I will not forget. Muchas gracias!

I'm going to describe what was a terrible experience for me. My cat got food poisoning and was vomiting terribly. I took him in at 4 a.m., and the women who saw him were kind, although we later realized they had done more tests than necessary, since some were unnecessary. The next day, the poor thing went crazy when he saw me. When they told me he had to stay longer because he wasn't eating and they wouldn't discharge him, I gave him a piece of food, which he ate completely, along with some canned food, even though his stomach was obviously in terrible shape. When I mentioned that I knew someone who was knowledgeable about this, everyone at the vet's office completely changed their attitude. They became hostile and spoke to me differently. On top of all this, they did an ultrasound and told me several things: that the back of his intestine wasn't clearly visible, and that it wasn't clear if he had any linear bodies—basically, everything was designed to scare me. When I told them I was taking my cat and would come right back if he seemed unwell, there were looks and words that implied I was a bad owner. In fact, every employee was at the counter when I went to pay, giving me dirty looks. They even brought him upstairs without saying a word and told me, "You've walked right past him several times and didn't see him," even though I was a nervous wreck about him and what had happened. One employee even offered me some advice in a different tone when no one else was listening. Months have passed, and the animal didn't have to go back. He needed my love and care, and after just a few days of intensive care at home, he recovered. They were just trying to run more tests and have him hospitalized in the emergency room, which is expensive. THE PRACTICES OF THIS PLACE ARE DISGUSTING. DON'T TAKE YOUR PET THERE IF YOU DON'T WANT TO BE RIPPED OFF. THEY DON'T CARE ABOUT THEIR HEALTH, ONLY THE MONEY!!!

I want to thank Estrella, who took wonderful care of my little hippie dog, and the cardiologist at the clinic; both were professional, kind, and sweet at all times.

I highly recommend them.
Thanks to the FIP diagnosis that other veterinarians failed to make, we saved my kitten

Our beloved Xofi passed away yesterday.
We didn't know where to turn, and someone told us about this clinic. We were treated with so much kindness and empathy. I recommend it without hesitation; they are wonderful professionals ❤️

If you love your pet, you'd better read this;
First, they vaccinated my cat with an EXTRA vaccine. The vet wasn't the usual one and didn't check her vaccination record before vaccinating her, and they still tried to charge me. Even though I insisted that the doctor or specialist vaccinated my cat without checking her previous vaccinations, they still charged me, supposedly with a "discount," even though the mistake wasn't mine... Then yesterday, I took my cat to the clinic because she has a red eye, and they weren't able to see her because "the specialist wasn't there." So what's the point of being a 24-hour clinic? Why should I bring my pet in for an emergency if you can't treat her? The vets wanted to give me an appointment for the next day... I asked if they could prescribe something to soothe the itching, and they agreed to give me something to calm the cat, but of course, without a diagnosis and without even seeing her. The conclusion is that I'd rather not buy the prescription and take her somewhere else… The girls are very nice, and the place is pretty, but it's not the best place for an emergency.
Correct diagnosis and they fulfilled what I came for.
The worst vet clinic. Very bad service….
I'm a regular customer at the hair salon; they're always great, especially Lourdes, the hairdresser. She's a very good professional and makes my poodle, Coffee, look super handsome.

Our cat, Cookie was brought to Animalia late at night after a serious fall. We arrived shortly afterwards and paid over €600 for her emergency treatment and 24 hours of hospitalisation.

From the beginning, the communication was chaotic and contradictory. The first thing that shocked us was that although we had paid for 24 hours of hospitalisation, nobody ever told us Cookie had to be collected by 7pm the following day or we would automatically be charged for another full day. We only found this out because a family member called the hospital for us, as neither of us speaks Spanish fluently.

Knowing she would be discharged at 7pm, we asked for Cookie's medical records at around 2pm so we could send them to other veterinarians for a second opinion before making any life changing decisions. The records never arrived. We chased them repeatedly by phone for hours while the discharge deadline got closer and closer. By the time they finally came through, we had almost run out of time. Whether intentional or not, it prevented us from getting another opinion before having to decide what to do.

The biggest issue, however, was the complete contradiction in what we were told. Earlier that same day we were told Cookie's breathing was fine. We were told we were free to take her home if we wanted to seek another opinion. Her leg had already been bandaged and Animalia were not even planning to operate that day or the next. Surgery was going to be several days later anyway. So, keeping her hospitalised would simply have meant paying for additional days while waiting.

Then, when we arrived to collect her at 7pm, everything changed. We were suddenly told her breathing was extremely serious and that she could die if we took her home.

Being told your kitten could die is one of the worst things you can hear. We were terrified. What we still cannot understand is how her breathing apparently went from "fine" to "she could die if you take her home" within just a few hours.

The following day we took Cookie to another veterinarian for a second opinion. He repeated the X rays, examined her thoroughly and listened carefully to her chest. His conclusion was completely different. He told us Cookie was outside any danger relating to her lungs and was not concerned about her breathing. He also told us that recommending surgery after looking at only one X ray view, without a more thorough assessment or considering Cookie's young age and healing potential, was not how he would have approached the case.

We were never properly presented with different treatment options at Animalia. We were made to feel surgery was the only realistic choice. When we asked if there were any alternatives, we were told, "Well, there's always amputation." Hearing those words about a 7 month old kitten was heartbreaking.

We were also told Cookie's "massive" open wound carried a very high risk of infection. Less than 24 hours later, the second vet found the wound had already dried significantly, was healing very well and was not considered to be at significant risk of infection. He treated her with wound cream and natural pain relief. A couple of days later, the wound is almost completely dry and barely visible.

I understand that veterinary medicine is not always black and white and that different vets can recommend different treatments. What I cannot accept is being told one thing in the morning and something completely different in the evening, especially when the second opinion less than 24 hours later contradicted so many of the warnings we had been given. The entire experience left us feeling that we had been frightened into believing there was only one safe option: more hospitalisation and an expensive surgery.

Thankfully, Cookie is now recovering well under another veterinarian's care without surgery.

If you are are told your pet urgently needs a major procedure here, seek a second opinion before making that decision. We are incredibly grateful that we did.

My experience was a year ago, and it was terrible. My dog ​​was hospitalized because she ate a piece of baseboard, and she died during surgery. They called me with the news, and then an hour and a half later, they called again to say they had resuscitated her. My dog ​​was never the same. She had been without oxygen for 10 minutes, and over the following days, everything started failing. She went blind, developed a heart murmur, her blood pressure skyrocketed, and so on. We learned all of this from another vet because we took her from Mi Vet, and they didn't give us much hope. She was so ill; it was as if she weren't herself anymore, and in the end, we decided to have her euthanized. It was all so painful, losing my little dog. This pain will always be with us.
Whenever I've had an emergency with my dog, I go to them; they're professionals.

A veterinarian who goes to do business with medicine for a dog with an allergic outbreak does not love animals. It is Sunday, we have a prescription from our veterinarian, from Friday afternoon, it is very hot and we have come without the dog. The medicine is not available in any pharmacy, we are desperate and we come all the way here… we know that the box costs €2.50, the girl at the reception as a “favor” (cloth… because we have a prescription!!) has sold us a blister pack (there are 3 in the box) for €15.90. I ask her, is that the price of a blister pack? She smiles. I thank her. In the end, I do love my dog. They have charged 636% more than the pharmacy price.

Thank you for your review, Valentina! 💙
We're so glad to hear your experience with our team was positive. 🐾

Thank you for your trust!
24-hour service
Good professionals and friendly

We went to the vet in the middle of the night with our dog and we couldn't be more grateful for the care we received. Both Estrella and her colleague were incredibly kind, attentive, and professional at all times. They gave us a very thorough examination, calmly checking everything and explaining every detail clearly and calmly, which gave us a great deal of peace of mind. It's wonderful to find people like that in times of worry. Thank you so much for your care and kindness.

Àris needed surgery for a lump on her leg and we didn't know if there was anything else. They operated on her incredibly, they visited her several times because her stitches were coming out and, in the end, everything went perfectly. She is completely recovered and is back to her old self.
Thank you all so much, you are incredible as professionals and as people.
❤️❤️❤️

Two years ago we brought our dog in the morning in a very serious condition (we didn't know it at the time). They did an X-ray and told us to leave her there, that the vet would come later, they didn't tell us that she was in a serious condition, although later talking to other vets they told us that the symptoms and the results of the X-rays were very serious. They told us to go to work calmly. After two hours they called us saying that her heart had stopped, we couldn't say goodbye. I don't recommend her because of the negligence we encountered.

I visited Animalia for an emergency consultation and was initially very pleased with the care. The doctor was attentive, took a detailed history, and even had an ophthalmologist check my dog's eyes to rule out vision-related issues.

However, after his initial assessment, he recommended I move to a larger hospital with more advanced machinery for an in-depth analysis. While I appreciated his honesty, I specifically questioned if we could start with something more basic, like a 4DX parasite test. He suggested it would be better to do all tests at once at the specialized hospital to avoid stressing her.

I understand that logic, but I am giving 3 stars because this resulted in my dog having to undergo the same physical and ophthalmic exams all over again at the second hospital (which stressed her...). Ultimately, it was the 50€ 4DX test I had originally asked for that confirmed Ehrlichia.

I wish the doctor had trusted my instincts and the discussions I had regarding her history before immediately dispatching us to a 'better hospital.' An emergency consultation is not cheap, and I expected more basic diagnostics to be performed before being referred elsewhere. That said, I do appreciate the team's kindness and the fact that they even called a cab for us.
Good vet and good hairdresser

Hello Paula,
Please tell us what happened by writing to animalia@mivet.com, including a phone number so we can contact you.

Mivet Animalia Veterinary Team

I came from quite a distance to buy a can of gastrointestinal food for my kitten who has diarrhea and you didn't want to sell it to me because it's a holiday and you don't consider it an emergency. For me it was an emergency. Frankly SHAMEFUL

I always come here for my cats and I feel very safe and well cared for. They are very knowledgeable and always very kind and have your cats' best interests at heart. In this case, Pablo was very patient and guided us perfectly through the process of treating the cystitis one of them had. A true professional. I am very grateful.

Many thanks to the entire team, and especially to David, for the wonderful care you gave our dog Dora during her surgery last June, her hospital stay, and all the checkups she's had since. If it weren't for you, Dora wouldn't be here! THANK YOU!

We are very happy with this veterinary clinic. We chose it because it's very close to our home, but we've stayed because they've always treated us wonderfully. Lately, we've been taking our dog, Trufa, there a lot for dermatological problems, and Laura has been a fantastic professional.
We came for an emergency on a Sunday at 1 p.m. and it's closed. Please update your opening hours.
I'm editing my review because, frankly, the staff at reception have lost their friendliness lately, and it hasn't returned in a long time. It's a shame.
Thank you so much for your review, Lina! 💙 We're so glad to hear you're happy with our team and the service you received. 🐾 …
The dog grooming at this place is fantastic, I'm very happy with the results. I highly recommend it, Lourdes is very friendly!

This clinic is incredibly expensive, and because it's the only one covered by the national health service, they charge almost double the price for medications! Don't buy anything here, it's outrageous!!! There are clinics in Sants with medications for almost half the price! You just have to walk a bit further. Awful.
As I feared, Mivet Animalia has lost its best veterinarians. I've lost my trusted vet, and honestly, it's not what it used to be. It's a shame.

I went to the emergency room because my cat had an accident, and they were incredibly professional, as well as being incredibly kind and empathetic with both me and my pet. Having your pet spend the night in a hospital injured, intubated, and at risk of death is never a pleasant or easy experience, but thanks to the excellent service they provided, I felt confident that the situation was in good hands. And it was. My cat is recovering well, and I will always be grateful for the great work they did. Thank you for everything.

I don't know whether to call them an emergency after a two-hour wait. My dog ​​arrived with something stuck in his throat. Normally, they explain the situation to customers. When I called five minutes early to ask if they were handling emergencies, a guy arrived with an anesthetized cat and a girl with another small dog right after me. They were seen immediately. I don't know if it's because I'm a little worried about my dog, but I get the feeling I didn't receive the same attention as the other reviews. I absolutely do not recommend this place for emergencies. It's not a matter of anxiety. When you enter, they ask if you have a record with them. They should also explain how long it will take so you can decide whether to take your dog somewhere else and avoid these kinds of misunderstandings. I've seen that I'm not the only one complaining about the wait in the emergency room. I suggest they communicate how "their system works." After two hours, my dog ​​won't be the case, but don't assume that after two hours, you know how their system works. And I even called to ask to avoid things like this.
Very poor service in the emergency room; if I could give it 0 stars I would.

They should have a support network, as pets require immediate attention not only for their health but also for their owners' peace of mind, thus avoiding further problems. It's unbelievable that my friend's pet has been waiting for over an hour and they haven't attended to her. Her dog keeps vomiting and they just keep making her wait. Terrible service.
3 hours with the poor dog, it's 8:00 and we're still waiting. If he dies it will be your fault.
I don't know how someone can arrive in an emergency and have the dog agonizing for two hours without receiving medical attention.

On the 25th, we had to take our dog Lola to the emergency vet. Sadly, we had to put her to sleep. I want to thank Laia, the veterinarian who treated us, for her empathy, gentleness, and professionalism during such a difficult time. I will definitely continue to take my animals to this clinic.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM for end-of-life matters. My dog ​​was diagnosed with cancer, and I was told that when the time came for euthanasia, we would only need to make an appointment. They assured me in my dog's final days that it was completely justified. However, when we made the appointment, they gave us a normal visit, telling us that his treatment would have to be changed, and we were like, "Do you even know why we're here?" It turns out that, due to the vet's morals that day, she wasn't going to perform the euthanasia. This was incredibly difficult for us, having to prepare for that moment. It's more than clear that they don't have a protocol to follow in these situations; they lack professional judgment. The very next day, the vet who had initially told me that euthanasia was COMPLETELY justified called me and said she had changed her mind and that more tests needed to be done. You can't change my mind with something like this. The dog was already very sick, the pain medication wasn't even working anymore, what more tests did they want? They told me they would speak to the person in charge there so he could call me the next day and assess whether to perform euthanasia. I told them I started work at a specific time, so they had to call me before then. I left for work early to be calm and avoid being on the subway. It was 10 minutes before I had to start and no one had called me. I ended up calling myself, and they kept saying he was in a meeting and so on. Knowing the situation and the whole mess surrounding the case, and how badly your colleagues handled it, you should at least have some consideration and call when you need to, if only out of a little respect. This man never answered the phone; he passed the message on to the person who was helping me at that moment. It took him just as long to tell me as it did to pass the message on. That's how considerate they were, and how important the matter was to them. Apparently, for them, talking about this 5 minutes before starting work is perfectly normal. I went in, obviously devastated and crying, because they weren't making it easy for me on the phone either. In the end, I found another veterinary clinic where they assessed my dog's condition. They performed some simple tests (not the ones they had requested), and the next day my little dog died. I wouldn't have wanted to see him the way I saw him in his final days; I think it was something that could have been prevented. But at least he passed away peacefully and surrounded by loved ones.

Choosing a veterinarian is always complicated; situations are often very difficult, and you'll find both positive and negative experiences at every clinic.

In my case, I can only describe how well we were treated. We knew our dog's condition was terminal, but they treated him with such gentleness that we were truly grateful. They were also flexible and very compassionate with us. I would emphasize that they prioritized good care over profit, which is always a sensitive issue when it comes to veterinarians. I can only express my gratitude to this hospital, and I would definitely return if needed.

First of all, I'm sorry to have to report this situation. After 15 years of trusting you with my pet Coco, and before that, 13 years with Guizmo,

Last Friday, December 12th, I needed to contact Sergio Perucho because the palliative medication he had prescribed for Coco two months prior wasn't working or agreeing with him. Therefore, he needed an adjustment, more medication, or a change of medication altogether.

I called at 9:00 AM, as he himself told me I could call anytime if I needed help, but then the day I needed him, he didn't help me, and that's why I'm explaining why.
It was already 2:30 PM, and seeing that no one was calling or answering the phone, I decided to go in person.

When I arrived, he was on the street talking on the phone and NOT WORKING.

At reception, they told me to wait and that he would see me.

After waiting for over an hour, he didn't even bother to see me in person. He just told me, quickly and without any real care, that the medication was fine and that I should wait until Monday or Tuesday for an appointment.
I asked if another vet could see me, but that wasn't possible either. I just wanted to alleviate Coco's discomfort and suffering.
At that moment, I counted five vets wandering around the premises, talking amongst themselves and with the receptionists (they were having trouble with the till and were criticizing another colleague). When I asked if I had to leave without any solution, the receptionist told me yes, and that we all came in the same boat and in a hurry...very empathetic. (It's worth noting that this is a 24-hour emergency clinic, so if we have an emergency, we go there for help).
Well, I told her I would go somewhere else, and she thought that was fine. Obviously, I went to another vet, and by 6:30 pm Coco had already been seen and was on new medication. They're monitoring him in case it needs adjusting, and to this day he hasn't had any more seizures. So, clearly, a 15-year-old dog with a neurological condition like dementia was being mismedicated.

I knew from other pet owners that they're very poorly regarded in the area, and now I understand why.

I won't be going back, and when I do give them a recommendation, it won't be good.
If you're a vet and you work without being involved, you lose clients. If you don't provide care or you just do it to get it over with, you lose clients. And if you don't know about diseases in senior dogs, you lose clients.
In short, because of the mistreatment, inefficiency, lack of empathy, responsibility, sensitivity, and respect towards us and especially towards the dog, as well as the pain and distress the whole situation caused me, I'm writing this so that others know.

Sincerely, Eulália.

First of all, I'm sorry to have to report this situation after 15 years of trusting you with my pet Coco and before that, 13 years with Guismo.

Last Friday, December 12th, I needed to contact Sergio Perucho because the palliative medication he had prescribed two months prior wasn't working for Coco and needed adjusting.
I called at 9:00 AM (he himself says you can call "whenever we need something"... just to ignore it, of course).
At 2:30 PM, seeing that no one was calling and no one was answering the phone, I decided to go in person.
When I arrived, he was on the street talking on the phone, NOT WORKING.
At reception, they told me to wait and that he would see me.
After waiting for more than an hour, he didn't even bother to speak to me in person, saying that the medication was fine and that I should wait until Monday or Tuesday when they would give me an appointment.

I asked if another vet could see me, but that wasn't possible either. I just wanted to alleviate Coco's discomfort and suffering.

At that moment, I counted five vets walking around the premises, talking amongst themselves and with the receptionists (they were having trouble with the till and were criticizing another colleague). When I asked if I had to leave without any solution, the young woman told me yes, and that we were all in the same boat and in a hurry...very empathetic.

Well, I told her I would go somewhere else, and she thought that was fine.
I should mention that by 6:30 pm, Coco had already been seen and was on new medication. They are monitoring him to adjust it, and to this day, he hasn't had any more seizures, so I deduce that he was also on the wrong medication.
I knew from other pet owners that they are very poorly regarded in the area, and now I understand why.
I won't be going back, and word of mouth won't be good either.

Eulalia

We went to the emergency vet because our dog was having trouble breathing, coughing up a lot of mucus, and trembling. They attended to us incredibly quickly and were very kind. It's a shame we didn't ask for the name of the woman who treated us so we could acknowledge her excellent care and professionalism. Regarding the comments I saw about them "ripping off the public," etc.... Honestly, I don't know where people usually go, but for an emergency service, diagnosis, injection, and treatment on a Sunday morning, the price didn't seem inflated to me; it seemed quite fair. Best regards.

I have been coming here for ages because it is the closest vet to me. My dog has severe anxiety and its the only vet I could get him to. But after 4 years of trying to get him treatment for a number of issues, constant itching, severe anxiety, hip issues... they have never given him a second thought. I never see the same vet twice and every time I go they are completely appethetic and don't have any care or proactive presence with my very fearful dog. They never have specialists in house and I always have to ask them the same questions over and over which they just dismiss telling me they don't think anything is wrong or that they don't know what is wrong. They are completely useless and don't care at all about the wellbeing of animals. They even refused to do a basic nail clipping for my dog when I requested it. Its extremely disappointing and I feel very little support from anyone there.
Telephone, just for show. A disaster.

I took my dog ​​to get his annual vaccination yesterday. He's never had any reactions before, so I was extremely worried to see his face visibly swollen during the night and vomiting several times in the afternoon. When I called for advice, not only did they offer no solution, but the explanations I received were completely inadequate: that he might have been bitten by a spider or mosquito, or that the vomiting was probably because he'd eaten something that didn't agree with him.

Furthermore, the receptionist didn't know how to help me or provide even basic information, to the point that the veterinarian had to intervene several times. This demonstrates a worrying lack of training and professionalism. I'm not an expert; that's precisely why I go to a veterinary clinic, expecting a competent response and not unfounded assumptions.

Frankly, I don't think the negative reviews you have are a coincidence. I believe you don't have a sufficiently qualified team, and that's evident from the phone service to the resolution of even a simple case. Regarding the prices, although I find them exorbitant, I don't usually skimp when it comes to my dog's health. But paying so much for so little help is disappointing.

I'm very disappointed with the center and the staff. I would recommend you seriously review who you hire and the type of care you're providing.
The worst people I've ever met, utterly inhuman, all they care about is money; the worst experience of my life

We want to express our heartfelt gratitude to Gemma Pujol for the care she gave us just over three hours ago, when we arrived very worried about our 14-year-old beagle, Gin, who was trembling, panting, and extremely lethargic.

From the moment we arrived, we felt cared for: we were attended to with speed, professionalism, and above all, compassion that gave us immense peace of mind.
Gemma examined Gin with such care and gentleness that we felt he was in the best hands. She listened to us, calmly asked all the necessary questions, and instilled tremendous confidence in us during a difficult time. We are truly grateful for how well she cared for Gin.

Angela (and the whole team) is amazing 🥰 Thank you so much for taking care of Marie and making it possible for her to have a good quality of life. Despite having fibrosarcoma, she stays as healthy as possible! …

We took our cat in because she'd had sores around her neck since August that kept coming back and going.
They examined her (without gloves) and used a fungal lamp (they didn't see the fleas, for crying out loud!) and took a sample for microscopic examination. Diagnosis: Fungal infection (ringworm), "weak presentation." Shampoo and antibiotics (almost €70).
Ringworm is contagious. Since August, she hasn't infected anyone... and we sleep with her. Two days into the treatment, we saw fleas jumping around her neck. We had to shave her and buy flea treatments, etc. They could have given her oral antibiotics. They told me to start with topical antibiotics (to rip you off) and that they're two different things. But they didn't see the fleas... In short, a rip-off!! The shampoo was unnecessary... €150...

This clinic has become a money-making machine. I've been going for years, but you have to pay for the roadside rental in Sans, and today was my last day. First, they explain the tests to be done and the cost (most of them unnecessary) without even examining the animal. It's the complete opposite! I see there are many complaints about how this clinic has become a money-grab, which doesn't surprise me. I suppose there are excellent veterinarians, but if, as in my case, to diagnose gastroenteritis they have to do an ultrasound, blood tests, admit you for a day, and take an X-ray, you don't need to be a veterinarian (no abdominal exam, no temperature check, nothing like that). By the way, don't even think about mentioning that you called at least six times this morning and the answering machine picked up. If you say anything, they'll treat you like an idiot, saying you must have dialed the wrong number. In short, a disaster.

Since Animalia ceased to be a place that simply makes money and rushes to get another dog in, I'm very disappointed with the care my dog ​​Nena received. All I saw was a desire to make money and a complete lack of sensitivity. I've been a client of Animalia for 20 years, and since Mivet took over, it's pathetic. The receptionists, the new veterinarians—everything in general—is terrible. Only Anna is truly worthwhile as a veterinarian, and if she's ever not there, I wouldn't go back for anything. It's a real shame, considering how pleasant, friendly, and welcoming it used to be.

In response to your very specific message, I still feel the same way. Neither the treatment nor the empathy towards our pets is what it used to be, and as for the former staff, only the old owner and little else remains of Animalia.

I want to thank the former team for those 20 years of security and trust in the care they provided to both my pets and me.

Best regards.

The importance of charging us immediately after the loss of our beloved dog was appalling. They showed a lack of humanity by not waiting for us to grieve in peace for our pet. A lack of empathy and sensitivity during such a painful time. We understand that we have to pay for a service like euthanasia, but they should improve their human skills in such a difficult situation for us. WE RECOMMEND NOT TAKING YOUR PET TO THIS PLACE.

I must confess that it was difficult for me to write this review, as they were our trusted veterinarians for almost our beloved cat Christie's entire life. We always felt well cared for. Until our kitten started getting very ill. Then they became a money-making machine (always charging double the price because it was urgent, but we had to chase them down for the results) and some invoices were riddled with errors, charging us for tests that weren't performed. Once they had the fatal diagnosis (terminal cancer), they abandoned us because they didn't have a specialist (basically, "figure it out yourself"). They only coordinated with an external oncologist who advised them free of charge on the treatment plan, and only because we insisted... and then they told us that to get that information we had to pay for an urgent visit... but they got it for free! Again with the bill... after the fortune we spent in just three days. Very little empathy, very little professionalism, zero follow-up after the devastating diagnosis, no communication with the guardians in such an extreme and vulnerable situation, where we were left completely helpless and with time running out. Rest in peace, Gata Christie, thank goodness we were able to say a proper goodbye.

On September 14, 2025, we arrived at the emergency room of that place with a kitten of about 25 days old. The kitten had been suffering from diarrhea and dehydration for three days due to mismanagement by a private individual. We explained everything at reception. Animals with less serious illnesses were seen ahead of us. After a two-hour wait, I alerted them that the kitten was panting and eventually vomited. They ignored us, not even taking a look. After almost four hours of waiting, they finally saw us. They examined him, gave us an estimate, and as a final step, the kitten received IV fluids—much too late. He died two hours after being seen. I will never go to that place again. And I know where I will go for an emergency if necessary.
They take a long time to send the results to the patients.

I took my dog ​​to the groomer and they returned her with many bald patches, her hair shorter than I asked for, some wounds, and a very bad haircut. I don't recommend them. I paid for a decent service, but I shouldn't have paid for the mess they made of her fur.

Find a good 24-hour vet so you don't have to come here in an emergency. If you love your pet, don't bring them here. They have zero empathy and are very business-oriented (it's a chain, so someone must be focused on the bottom line). The best person at the center is the community manager, who will surely reply and try to get a good review to maintain their rating. We are so sorry that our kitten paid the price for our lack of knowledge and was in such bad company in his final hours. 🤍
Thanks to Eva, wonderful help with the medications I needed
I could never be more grateful for how you treated and helped Alfredo. Thank you Nerea, Pablo, Martina, and especially you Sergi. You are not veterinarians, you are angels.

I took my sick cat to the emergency room, they took a long time to treat him, once in the room my cat was starting to convulse and the doctor was talking to me about the budget instead of stabilizing him, before taking him there was no guide to assess whether it was urgent to admit him, simply according to my criteria. All this preceded by having discharged him 16 hours earlier and then justifying himself with the fact that the illness is very unstable. When you see them treated with so much love and professionalism, a part of you (however small, because you always want your furry friends at home) finds peace when you have to leave them there. Five stars because there aren't any more. Thank you so much to everyone who took care of Garfield; seeing him back home playing with his sister as if nothing had happened is one of the best feelings anyone can have.

I want to thank the on-call team on Monday, July 21, 2025, for their professionalism, safety, and kindness during my greyhound's emergency. This is the worst clinic you could ever trust with your animals. They take everything lightly and are incredibly insensitive. The puppy died due to the lack of care from those who call themselves veterinarians; their only concern is making money from clients, regardless of whether the animal survives or not.

A PAINFUL EXPERIENCE THAT NO ONE SHOULD HAVE TO SUFFER.

Today, with all the pain I feel, I find the courage to write this. I've never done it before, but the loss of my kitten is worth the effort. I don't want anyone else to go through the suffering we are experiencing.

It all started on Saturday when we took our cat to the emergency vet because he wasn't urinating properly and was passing a few drops that looked bad. After an initial examination, they told us it seemed to be idiopathic cystitis. They admitted him and performed all sorts of tests: blood work, urinalysis, catheterization, among others. We made it clear that they should do everything necessary for his well-being, regardless of the cost.

The next day, they informed us that all the tests had come back normal, that it was just common idiopathic cystitis, and that there was nothing serious. They showed us the blood work and explained that everything was perfect. They prescribed a treatment: a pill in the morning and at night, plus a nighttime syrup. They assured us that would be enough.
Following their instructions to the letter, we gave him the medication as prescribed. But three days later, his condition worsened. Although he was urinating normally, he was now lethargic, listless, hiding away, as if he weren't alive. Something was wrong.
We took him back to the emergency room at noon. They admitted him again and ran more tests. At 5 p.m., we went for a follow-up visit, but what they told us left us in shock: coldly, they informed us that he had died. They showed us test results where all the values ​​were extremely high, and to our disbelief, they told us that the syrup they had prescribed had caused his death. ONLY THREE DAYS HAD PASSED!
We couldn't believe it. A healthy cat, only four years old, who had always been fine, had died in just three days. And worst of all: instead of taking responsibility, they blamed us.

We spent over €1,400 trusting that we were doing what was best for him, only to end up losing him. The most frustrating thing is that no one has been able to explain what really happened. The veterinarian who treated him simply told us that she didn't know what the other doctors had done and that she had done "what she could."
We are left with immense grief and a profound sense of helplessness. All we can do is warn other pet owners: do not take your animals to this clinic. Our experience has been terrible, and we hope that no one else has to go through a tragedy like this.

They're only interested in making money; they're loan sharks... Love for animals is nowhere near their priority. They're unprofessional, unwilling to work, the clinic is completely unhygienic, and the staff is extremely negligent. I absolutely cannot recommend this place; don't be fooled!

I went there with all the worries in the world for my puppy Milo, but in the end, it was just a scare. I'm so grateful that the hospital is open 24/7 at any time (we went on a Sunday night). The receptionist and the vet were understanding and very friendly, and they clearly understood that I was terrified, but instead of laughing or making fun of me (because they knew Milo had something common in puppies and that he would recover), they just comforted me and focused on making me feel better about Milo.

As a new dog mom, I couldn't find a reliable vet, and I needed something that was a bit more affordable. But this experience has made this my go-to place! The prices are very reasonable.

I had to take my dog ​​to the emergency vet because he wasn't feeling well.
The examination they gave him seemed quite superficial, and they didn't find anything wrong. They suggested he'd probably eaten something that disagreed with him and that it would pass quickly.

I went back to the clinic later that same day because I was very worried about my dog's condition. They told me I needed to be more patient and that, if I wanted, they could do some blood work for my own peace of mind. They did it, and the results showed everything was fine.

The next day, I took Mateo to my trusted vet, who, upon hearing the symptoms, was very concerned. She gave him a much more thorough examination, and after seeing the same blood work from the previous day, she concluded that he most likely had a severe infection. She suggested I stop the painkillers since they were masking the symptoms and prescribed antibiotics. My dog ​​started to improve very quickly.

They did give me attention, but I felt they weren't taking the situation seriously, and in the end, they didn't pay attention to the details. I'm left with a bad taste in my mouth from the experience.
